chunks: And from him, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Like it, and he said: 'There is no harm in giving him its value as one dirham.'

key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (the obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay Zakat al-Fitr in cash or its monetary value?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility in fulfilling Zakat al-Fitr by permitting the payment of its monetary value (qimah) rather than strictly providing food, specifically citing one dirham as a valid equivalent. This ruling highlights the early juristic understanding of substituting cash for kind, a view supported by many Shia scholars to accommodate practical needs during distribution. It underscores the principle that the obligation is satisfied by the value intended for the poor's sustenance.
